paper_metadata.title: Seizure outcomes following multilobar epilepsy surgery

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the source population (Cleveland Clinic), recruitment period (1994-2010), and specific inclusion/exclusion criteria. Baseline characteristics are well-documented in Table 1.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: A retrospective chart review of patients undergoing surgery for medically refractory epilepsy at the Cleveland Clinic Epilepsy Center from 1994 until 2010 was performed.
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly defined as patients from a specific tertiary epilepsy center.

items.reasoning: The study uses a comprehensive retrospective review of all patients meeting the surgical criteria at a major center.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure freedom) is defined using the validated Engel Class system and measured through a structured follow-up protocol.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Patients were classified as seizure free if they achieved an Engel class I at last follow-up. The primary outcome was the time to first seizure recurrence.
items.reasoning: The Engel classification is a standard, well-defined outcome in epilepsy surgery.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: All patients were seen at 6 weeks, 6 months (with a 2-h outpatient EEG), 1 year, and then yearly after surgery.
items.reasoning: Regular clinical follow-up combined with EEG provides a reliable assessment of seizure status.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: All patients were seen at 6 weeks, 6 months... 1 year, and then yearly after surgery.
items.reasoning: The follow-up schedule was standardized for all patients.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).
items.evidence_snippet: A univariate analysis was then performed... Variables with 10% significance on univariate analysis were then tested in a multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression model.
items.reasoning: Confounding was addressed in the analysis phase rather than the design phase (no matching/stratification).

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: With multivariate analysis, the type of resection (p = 0.03), preoperative auras (p = 0.03), an incomplete resection (0.03), and the presence of postoperative spikes (p = 0.0003) correlated with seizure recurrence.
items.reasoning: Multivariable Cox regression was used to adjust for multiple factors simultaneously.
